Pilgrimage

PIL-grim-ij — a pilgrimage is the journey a 'pilgrim' takes, usually for religious or deeply personal reasons. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Pilgrimage is a religious or spiritual journey, often to a sacred place.

Every year, thousands of believers undertake a pilgrimage to the ancient temple on the mountain.

Worked Example

A woman spends her entire life savings and six weeks walking hundreds of miles across a foreign country, visiting sacred sites along the way, in order to fulfill a lifelong spiritual goal she has held since childhood.

That long, deeply meaningful journey undertaken for spiritual reasons is exactly what a pilgrimage is. Unlike 'vacation,' which is for rest and enjoyment, pilgrimage is undertaken specifically for religious or spiritual purpose.

How Pilgrimage Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

quest

quest: a long journey undertaken for an important purpose

spiritual journey

spiritual journey: a trip undertaken for religious or personal growth

trek

trek: a long, arduous journey, often on foot

Antonyms

casual outing

casual outing: a short, relaxed trip with no deeper purpose

errand

errand: a short, practical task or trip

How Strong Is It? — trek → quest → pilgrimage

trek vs. pilgrimage

trek vs. pilgrimage: Trek is a more general word than pilgrimage -- a trek can be taken for adventure or exercise alone, while pilgrimage always carries a specific religious or spiritual purpose.

quest vs. pilgrimage

quest vs. pilgrimage: Quest can feel broader than pilgrimage: pilgrimage is always a physical journey to a sacred place, while quest can describe any determined pursuit, physical or not.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — peregr-

root — peregr-: foreign, traveling abroad (Latin (peregrinus, from per- + ager, 'through the field/land'))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin peregrinus meant 'foreigner, one traveling abroad,' built from per- ('through') and ager ('field, land'). A pilgrimage is, at its root, a journey through foreign land undertaken for a meaningful purpose.

Use the root in a new word: peregrine

Use the root in a new word: peregrine: The peregrine falcon is famous for traveling incredible distances during its yearly migration.
